# Electric Vehicle Powertrain with Integrated CVT and Drive Motor Control

## Overview

The disclosed systems and methods relate to an electric vehicle (EV) powertrain that couples a continuously variable transmission (CVT) to an electric drive motor. By integrating these two components, the powertrain architecture enables a more flexible and efficient transfer of power from the electric drive motor to the wheels, allowing the vehicle to adapt dynamically to a wide range of operating conditions.

## Integrated Control System

Central to the disclosed powertrain is a control system configured to manage the CVT and/or the drive motor in order to optimize various efficiencies associated with the EV and its subsystems. Rather than treating the transmission and motor as independent components, the control system coordinates their operation, ensuring that each subsystem contributes to the overall performance and efficiency of the vehicle. This holistic approach allows the powertrain to respond intelligently to changing demands from the driver and the environment.

## Economy Mode Operation

When operating in economy mode, the control system simultaneously manages both the CVT and the drive motor to optimize the vehicle's range. By jointly regulating these components, the system minimizes energy losses and maximizes the distance the vehicle can travel on a given charge. This coordinated management is particularly advantageous for extending range, as it allows the powertrain to operate within the most efficient regions of the motor's performance map while maintaining smooth and responsive vehicle behavior.

## Control Mechanisms

To achieve these efficiency gains, the control system can regulate the current or power provided to the drive motor while also adjusting the transmission speed ratio of the CVT. By modulating the electrical input to the motor in concert with the mechanical ratio of the transmission, the system is able to deliver the required torque and speed at the wheels using the least amount of energy. This dual-parameter control provides a greater degree of freedom than conventional fixed-ratio EV powertrains, enabling finer optimization of the operating point.

## Adaptive Decision-Making

The control system makes its adjustments by taking into account a variety of factors, including battery voltage, throttle position, and transmission speed ratio. By continuously monitoring these inputs, the system can accurately assess both the driver's intent and the current state of the powertrain, and then determine the optimal combination of motor input and transmission ratio. This feedback-driven approach ensures that the powertrain remains responsive to real-time conditions while consistently pursuing the desired efficiency and range objectives.

# Electric Vehicle Powertrain with Continuously Variable Transmission and Integrated Control System

## Field of the Invention

The present disclosure relates generally to electric vehicle (EV) powertrains, and more particularly to systems and methods for optimizing the efficiency and driving range of an electric vehicle through the coordinated control of a continuously variable transmission (CVT) and an electric drive motor.

## Background

Electric vehicles rely on stored electrical energy to power one or more electric motors that propel the vehicle. A persistent challenge in the design and operation of such vehicles is the maximization of driving range for a given battery capacity. While conventional electric vehicles often employ fixed-ratio or single-speed transmissions, these configurations can force the electric drive motor to operate outside of its most efficient speed and torque regions across various driving conditions. As a result, energy is expended less efficiently, and the vehicle's overall range is diminished. There exists a need for a powertrain architecture and control strategy that can dynamically adapt to changing driving demands while keeping the drive motor operating near its peak efficiency.

## Summary of the Invention

The present disclosure provides systems and methods for an electric vehicle powertrain that features a continuously variable transmission (CVT) mechanically coupled to an electric drive motor. Rather than treating the transmission and the motor as independently controlled subsystems, the disclosed approach employs an integrated control system that simultaneously manages both the CVT speed ratio and the drive motor current. By coordinating these two variables in concert, the system is able to place the drive motor at an operating point that yields the greatest possible efficiency for the torque and speed demanded by the driver at any given moment.

## Detailed Description

In accordance with the disclosed embodiments, the electric vehicle powertrain includes an electric drive motor configured to provide propulsion torque, a continuously variable transmission coupled between the drive motor and the vehicle's driven wheels, and a control system in communication with both the transmission and the motor. The CVT is capable of adjusting its speed ratio in a continuous, stepless manner, allowing the effective gear ratio between the motor and the wheels to be varied across a broad range.

The control system is configured to receive a plurality of input signals representative of the vehicle's operating state. These inputs may include, among others, the battery voltage, the throttle position (reflecting the driver's demand for torque or acceleration), and the current transmission speed ratio. Based on these and other parameters, the control system determines target values for both the CVT speed ratio and the drive motor current.

A key feature of the disclosed system is the provision of an economy mode of operation. When the economy mode is engaged, the control system prioritizes energy efficiency and the maximization of driving range over other performance considerations. In this mode, the control system coordinates the CVT speed ratio and the drive motor current in a manner that keeps the drive motor operating within, or as close as possible to, its region of highest efficiency. For a given power demand, there are typically multiple combinations of motor speed and motor torque that can satisfy that demand; by adjusting the CVT ratio, the control system can select the combination that corresponds to the lowest energy consumption, and it can simultaneously regulate the motor current to deliver the required torque at that operating point.

The determination of the optimal operating point may account for a variety of interrelated factors. The battery voltage informs the control system of the available electrical energy and can influence the efficiency of the motor and associated power electronics. The throttle position conveys the driver's instantaneous demand, allowing the system to balance responsiveness against efficiency. The transmission speed ratio, together with vehicle speed, establishes the relationship between motor speed and wheel speed. By evaluating these factors together, the control system continuously computes and commands the pairing of CVT ratio and motor current that best serves the objective of extending range.

## Advantages

By simultaneously coordinating the continuously variable transmission and the electric drive motor rather than controlling them in isolation, the disclosed systems and methods enable the electric vehicle to maximize its driving range for a given amount of stored energy. Because the CVT can continuously adjust the effective gear ratio, the drive motor is not constrained to operate at inefficient points dictated by a fixed ratio; instead, it can be held near its peak-efficiency region across a wide spectrum of vehicle speeds and load conditions. The economy mode further ensures that, when range is the priority, the powertrain is operated in the most energy-conserving manner consistent with the driver's demands.

The result is an improvement in overall vehicle performance and energy efficiency. The integrated control strategy delivers smoother power delivery, reduced energy consumption, and an extended driving range, thereby addressing the longstanding need for more efficient and capable electric vehicle powertrains.

# Understanding the Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT)

The **Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT)** represents one of the most significant innovations in modern automotive engineering. Unlike traditional automatic or manual transmissions that shift between a fixed number of gears, a CVT provides a seamless range of gear ratios, allowing the engine to run more efficiently.

## Operating Principle

The **operating** mechanism of a CVT is fundamentally different from conventional systems. Most CVTs use a pair of variable-diameter pulleys connected by a steel belt or chain. As the vehicle accelerates, one pulley expands while the other contracts, continuously adjusting the effective gear ratio. This smooth, stepless transition eliminates the "gear-hunting" sensation common in traditional automatics and keeps the engine **operating** within its optimal power band.

Because the CVT maintains ideal engine speed under varying conditions, it delivers improved fuel economy and reduced emissions. During steady cruising, the transmission holds a high ratio to minimize engine strain, while during acceleration it shifts toward lower ratios for maximum torque.

## Technical Details Disclosed

In numerous patents and engineering documents, the internal workings of the CVT have been thoroughly **disclosed** to help manufacturers refine performance and durability. These **disclosed** specifications typically cover:

- **Pulley geometry** and the range of achievable ratios
- **Belt or chain materials** engineered to withstand high tension
- **Hydraulic control systems** that manage pulley pressure
- **Software algorithms** that govern ratio selection based on driver input

By having these design elements clearly **disclosed**, engineers can build upon existing technology, ensuring reliability and continued advancement.

## Conclusion

The CVT continues to evolve as automakers seek greater efficiency without sacrificing driving comfort. With its unique **operating** characteristics and the wealth of technical knowledge **disclosed** across the industry, the CVT remains a cornerstone of contemporary vehicle design—offering drivers a smooth, responsive, and economical experience on the road.

The control system comprises one or more processors and sensors configured to monitor operating parameters including motor speed, torque demand, battery state-of-charge, vehicle velocity, and driver input.

The control system may employ predictive algorithms utilizing route data, topographical information, and historical driving patterns to preemptively adjust transmission ratios and motor output. In certain embodiments, the system coordinates regenerative braking with dynamic CVT ratio adjustment to enhance energy recovery during deceleration.

# Technical Summary: Integrated Control System for EV with CVT and Electric Motor

## System Overview

This document describes an integrated powertrain control system for an electric vehicle (EV) that coordinates the operation of a continuously variable transmission (CVT) and an electric traction motor. The system optimizes the interaction between motor torque delivery and transmission ratio selection to enhance efficiency, performance, and drivability, with a dedicated economy mode for maximizing driving range.

---

## 1. System Architecture

### 1.1 Core Components
- **Electric Traction Motor:** Provides primary propulsion torque; capable of regenerative braking.
- **Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT):** Enables infinitely variable gear ratios within a defined range, decoupling motor speed from wheel speed.
- **Powertrain Control Unit (PCU):** Central controller executing coordination algorithms.
- **Battery Management System (BMS):** Supplies state-of-charge (SOC), temperature, and power limit data.
- **Sensor Array:** Includes wheel speed sensors, throttle/pedal position, motor RPM, torque sensors, and CVT pulley position feedback.

### 1.2 Control Hierarchy
The PCU operates on a supervisory-subordinate architecture:
- **Supervisory Layer:** Interprets driver intent and mode selection; issues target torque and efficiency setpoints.
- **Subordinate Layer:** Executes real-time motor control (via inverter) and CVT ratio actuation.

---

## 2. Control Strategy

### 2.1 Torque and Ratio Coordination
The system continuously solves for the optimal combination of:
- **Motor operating point** (torque and rotational speed)
- **CVT ratio**

that satisfies the driver's requested wheel torque while minimizing total energy consumption. Because electric motors exhibit efficiency variation across their speed-torque map, the CVT is leveraged to keep the motor operating within its high-efficiency region for a given power demand.

### 2.2 Efficiency Optimization
An onboard efficiency model (motor efficiency map + CVT loss model) determines the ratio that yields the lowest combined losses. The controller balances:
- Motor electrical efficiency
- CVT mechanical/hydraulic losses
- Transient response requirements

---

## 3. Operating Modes

### 3.1 Standard (Normal) Mode
Balances responsiveness and efficiency. Ratio changes and torque delivery prioritize a natural driving feel while maintaining reasonable energy economy.

### 3.2 Performance Mode
Prioritizes acceleration and responsiveness. The CVT holds ratios that maximize available wheel torque, and torque-limiting constraints are relaxed within thermal and battery limits.

### 3.3 Economy Mode (Range Maximization)
The economy mode reconfigures control priorities to extend driving range:

- **Efficiency-First Operating Point:** The controller biases motor operation toward peak-efficiency zones, adjusting CVT ratio proactively rather than reactively.
- **Torque Rate Limiting:** Acceleration requests are smoothed to avoid high-loss transient events.
- **Optimized Regeneration:** Coordinates CVT ratio during deceleration to maximize energy recovery within motor and battery acceptance limits.
- **Speed-Aware Ratio Scheduling:** At cruising speeds, the CVT selects tall ratios to reduce motor RPM and associated losses.
- **Auxiliary Load Awareness:** Optionally integrates with vehicle systems to account for HVAC and accessory loads in the efficiency calculation.

---

## 4. Control Logic Flow

1. **Input Acquisition:** Read pedal position, vehicle speed, motor state, battery limits, and selected mode.
2. **Driver Intent Interpretation:** Convert pedal input into a target wheel torque request, scaled by mode.
3. **Optimization:** Compute the motor operating point and CVT ratio minimizing energy consumption subject to constraints (battery power limits, thermal limits, ratio bounds, drivability filters).
4. **Actuation:** Command inverter torque and CVT ratio actuator simultaneously and in coordination.
5. **Feedback and Correction:** Monitor actual response and apply closed-loop correction.

---

## 5. Constraints and Safety

- **Battery Limits:** Torque commands are bounded by available charge/discharge power from the BMS.
- **Thermal Protection:** Motor and CVT temperatures trigger derating when limits are approached.
- **Ratio Change Rate Limits:** CVT actuation is bounded to prevent mechanical stress and abrupt behavior.
- **Fault Handling:** Sensor faults default the system to a safe, limited-performance operating state.

---

## 6. Benefits

- Extended driving range via combined motor–transmission efficiency optimization
- Improved regenerative braking recovery through ratio coordination
- Configurable driving characteristics across selectable modes
- Reduced thermal stress by maintaining favorable motor operating points

---

*This summary describes system functionality at a conceptual level; specific implementation parameters (efficiency maps, control gains, ratio ranges, and thresholds) should be calibrated to the target vehicle platform.*

counterfactuals.output:
# EV Range Optimization: Coordinating CVT and Motor Current

Interesting question—though it's worth noting upfront that **most modern EVs don't use a CVT**, since electric motors have broad torque bands that make multi-speed transmissions largely unnecessary. However, some EVs and prototypes *do* use CVTs or multi-speed gearboxes to keep the motor in its efficient operating zone. Let me explain how such a coordinated system would work.

## Core Principle: Efficiency Mapping

The foundation is the motor's **efficiency map**—a plot of efficiency (%) across torque vs. RPM. Every electric motor has a "sweet spot" (often 90–97% efficiency) in a specific speed/load region, with efficiency dropping off at very low speeds, very high speeds, or extreme torque demands.

The goal in economy mode:
> Keep the motor operating near its peak-efficiency island as often as possible, regardless of vehicle speed.

## How Coordination Works

The CVT decouples **road speed** from **motor speed**, giving the controller a degree of freedom to optimize:

| Variable | Controlled by |
|----------|---------------|
| Wheel speed | Fixed by vehicle velocity |
| Motor RPM | Set by CVT ratio |
| Motor torque | Set by current command |
| Power delivered | Torque × speed (must meet driver demand) |

**The key insight:** For a given power demand at the wheels, there are *many* combinations of motor RPM and torque that satisfy it. The controller picks the combination with the lowest total losses.

## The Control Loop

1. **Determine power demand** from accelerator input, filtered/smoothed in economy mode to reject aggressive transients.

2. **Query the optimization function**: Given required wheel power and current speed, solve for the motor RPM (via CVT ratio) and current (torque) that minimizes combined losses:
   - Motor copper losses (∝ current²)
   - Iron/core losses (frequency-dependent)
   - Inverter switching losses
   - CVT mechanical/hydraulic losses

3. **Command the CVT ratio** to bring the motor toward the target RPM.

4. **Command inverter current** to produce the needed torque at that operating point.

5. **Iterate continuously** as conditions change.

## Why This Improves Range

- **Avoids high-current, low-speed operation**: At low road speeds, a fixed-ratio EV might run the motor slowly with high torque (high current → high I²R heating). A CVT lets the motor spin faster at lower torque, reducing copper losses.

- **Reduces field-weakening at high speed**: At high speeds, motors enter field-weakening (injecting current that produces no torque), which hurts efficiency. A CVT can keep motor RPM lower, avoiding this regime.

- **Smooths regenerative braking**: The CVT can position the motor at an efficient generating speed to recover more energy.

## The Central Trade-off

The controller must weigh **CVT losses against motor gains**:

```
Total loss = Motor/Inverter losses(RPM, torque) + CVT losses(ratio, torque)
```

A CVT typically costs 5–15% in mechanical efficiency. The coordination only helps net range if the motor efficiency gains **exceed** the transmission overhead—which is why direct-drive dominates in production EVs, but why CVTs can help for vehicles with wide speed ranges or motors with narrow efficiency islands (e.g., some commercial or performance applications).

## Practical Refinements

- **Predictive control**: Using GPS/route data to pre-position the ratio for upcoming hills or speed changes.
- **Thermal management**: Shifting operating points to keep motor/inverter within optimal temperature, since efficiency and loss limits are temperature-dependent.
- **Hysteresis and rate-limiting**: Preventing excessive CVT "hunting" that would waste energy and annoy the driver.

---

Would you like me to go deeper on any part—such as the loss-minimization math, the motor efficiency map details, or how this compares to a discrete 2-speed gearbox approach?

# PATENT APPLICATION

## SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR OPTIMIZING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN AN ELECTRIC VEHICLE EMPLOYING A CONTINUOUSLY VARIABLE TRANSMISSION AND ELECTRIC DRIVE MOTOR

---

### FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to electric vehicle powertrain systems, and more particularly to systems and methods for dynamically optimizing the operational efficiency of an electric vehicle incorporating a continuously variable transmission (CVT) operatively coupled to an electric drive motor.

---

### BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Electric vehicles conventionally employ single-ratio or fixed-ratio gear reduction assemblies interposed between an electric drive motor and one or more driven wheels. While such arrangements provide mechanical simplicity, they constrain the operating region of the electric drive motor to a fixed relationship relative to vehicle road speed, thereby preventing the motor from continuously operating within its region of peak electromechanical efficiency.

[0003] Electric motors exhibit efficiency characteristics that vary as a function of rotational speed and output torque, defining an efficiency map having one or more regions of maximal energy conversion efficiency. A fixed-ratio drivetrain compels the motor to traverse regions of suboptimal efficiency across the range of vehicle operating conditions, resulting in diminished energy utilization, reduced driving range, and accelerated depletion of an onboard energy storage device.

[0004] Accordingly, there exists a need in the art for a system and method that dynamically modulates a transmission ratio to maintain the electric drive motor within a preferred efficiency region across a broad range of operating conditions, thereby optimizing overall powertrain efficiency and extending vehicle range.

---

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present invention provides, in various embodiments, a system and method for optimizing operational efficiency in an electric vehicle. In one aspect, the system comprises an electric drive motor, a continuously variable transmission operatively coupled between the electric drive motor and a driven member, a plurality of sensors configured to generate operational data, and a controller configured to modulate a transmission ratio of the continuously variable transmission as a function of said operational data to maintain the electric drive motor within a predetermined efficiency region.

[0006] In another aspect, the invention provides a method comprising the steps of receiving operational data, determining a target transmission ratio based upon a stored efficiency map, and commanding an actuator to adjust the continuously variable transmission to substantially achieve said target transmission ratio.

[0007] It is an object of certain embodiments to extend the effective driving range of an electric vehicle by continuously maintaining the electric drive motor at or near a locus of peak efficiency.

[0008] It is a further object of certain embodiments to enable regenerative braking optimization by modulating the transmission ratio during deceleration events to maximize recovered energy.

[0009] The foregoing summary is illustrative and is not intended to limit the scope of the claims appended hereto.

---

### BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0010] FIG. 1 is a schematic block diagram illustrating a powertrain system according to an embodiment of the present invention.

[0011] FIG. 2 is a flowchart depicting a method of transmission ratio optimization according to an embodiment.

[0012] FIG. 3 is a graphical representation of an efficiency map utilized by the controller.

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

[0013] Reference will now be made in detail to certain embodiments of the invention, examples of which are illustrated in the accompanying drawings. The following description is provided by way of illustration and not by way of limitation. Those of ordinary skill in the art will recognize that numerous modifications and variations may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention.

**System Architecture**

[0014] In one embodiment, the system comprises: (a) an electric drive motor configured to receive electrical energy from an onboard energy storage device and to convert said electrical energy into mechanical rotational output; (b) a continuously variable transmission having an input member operatively coupled to said electric drive motor and an output member operatively coupled to a driven member, said continuously variable transmission being configured to provide an infinitely or substantially infinitely variable transmission ratio between a minimum ratio and a maximum ratio; (c) an actuator operatively associated with said continuously variable transmission and configured to modulate said transmission ratio in response to a control signal; (d) a plurality of sensors; and (e) a controller in communicative connection with said plurality of sensors and said actuator.

[0015] The continuously variable transmission may comprise, without limitation, a belt-and-variable-pulley arrangement, a toroidal traction-drive arrangement, a planetary continuously variable arrangement, or any functionally equivalent mechanism capable of providing continuous variation of the transmission ratio.

[0016] The plurality of sensors may include, without limitation, a motor speed sensor, a motor torque sensor, a vehicle speed sensor, an accelerator position sensor, a brake position sensor, a battery state-of-charge sensor, a temperature sensor, and a current sensor. Each sensor is configured to generate operational data representative of a respective monitored parameter and to transmit said operational data to the controller.

**Control Methodology**

[0017] The controller comprises a processor and a non-transitory computer-readable medium having stored thereon instructions that, when executed by the processor, cause the controller to perform the operations described herein. The controller further has stored thereon, or has access to, at least one efficiency map correlating electric drive motor operating parameters with corresponding energy conversion efficiency values.

[0018] In operation, the controller receives operational data from the plurality of sensors, including at least a demanded output parameter derived from the accelerator position sensor and a vehicle speed parameter. Based upon said operational data, the controller determines a demanded output power at the driven member.

[0019] The controller thereupon determines, by reference to the stored efficiency map, a target motor operating point comprising a target motor rotational speed and a target motor torque that (i) satisfy said demanded output power and (ii) correspond to a substantially maximal energy conversion efficiency achievable for said demanded output power.

[0020] The controller subsequently computes a target transmission ratio defined substantially by the relationship of said target motor rotational speed to a rotational speed of the output member as constrained by present vehicle speed, and generates a control signal commanding the actuator to modulate the continuously variable transmission toward said target transmission ratio.

[0021] In a further embodiment, the controller iteratively and continuously repeats said operations at a predetermined update interval such that the electric drive motor is maintained substantially within a predetermined efficiency region throughout dynamically varying operating conditions.
